mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as elevated inflation erodes real corporate profits and increases the risk of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above its 5-year median, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings contraction and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above their 12-month averages indicates an aggressive monetary tightening cycle amid persistent inflation, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month averages, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (as indicated by housing starts above 1.3 million units), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and the risk of policy tightening, leading to negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1300, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 155,000 thousand persons indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 155000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index, 2017=100) signals a contraction in manufacturing and services, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) below 650,000 million dollars indicates weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate sales growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS < 650000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
